rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 4-5 (Results, Cases 1-5, Figures 3-8) report the authors' own model runs of a linear-quadratic optimal control scheme coupled to a state-space soil-crop-climate model for maize on Panoche clay, producing hourly irrigation schedules over a 50-day horizon.
rows.notes: The study is a purely simulation-based optimal-control exercise: the controller output (irrigation rates, water use, percolation, salinity, shoot weight) is never compared with measurements from a real field. Case 1 is called a 'verification' only in the sense that the controller recovers the known 0.5 cm/d target; the authors state the results follow a priori expected patterns. Calibration/verification of the underlying crop model is attributed to earlier work (de Wit et al. 1978; Protopapas and Bras 1988), not reported here. The study does show, within the model, that high water cost reduces irrigation from 48 cm to 16 cm (Figures 3b, 4b), but per the rating rules an unvalidated simulation does not count as own evidence on water conservation. Authors note the model cannot account for inaccurate system representation and that climatic uncertainty is not considered (Section 6), but since Q2 is no these do not score.

rows.evidence: Q1: Section 5.3, Cases 2-5 (Figures 5-8) report the authors' own model runs in which the controller manages root-zone salinity (e.g., leaching 3000 mg/L to below 1000 mg/L with salt-free water in Case 3; stabilising salinity at 1000 mg/L in Case 4).
rows.notes: Salinity control is simulated with a lumped root-zone salt mass-balance model (Appendix, equations A8-A11) under hypothetical initial and irrigation-water salinities; no measured soil salinity from a real field is used to check the controller's outcome. The paper itself says the examples were chosen to test correct behaviour of the controller and that results can probably be guessed from experience. Hence no own empirical evidence on soil-health (salinity) outcomes of app-based scheduling; the study only demonstrates the method's feasibility in simulation.

notes: Full text appears complete (pp. 647-669) though OCR is garbled in places, especially equations and figure axes. The study is a deterministic optimal-control modelling paper with case-study simulations for maize on Panoche clay; no field data, surveys or model-versus-observation comparisons are reported, so both claim rows score Q1 yes, Q2 no.
